chunk_text: X Park is the country's first theme park dedicated to motorized and non-motorized extreme sports. Spread over 40 acres, X Park offers over 20 different activities that suit various ages and preferences. Get your adrenalin fix here with Flying Fox, Motocross, Go Kart, ATV, High Rope, Bubbleball Futsal, Skate Park and Paintball. Visitors also have ample choices for milder pursuits such as Aquawalk, Kayaking, Swan Boat Paddling and Glamping.

chunk_text:
A one-stop centre for art and crafts, this complex offers

the perfect opportunity to watch, learn and participate in the various art forms of Johor. Exuding a Malay village-style ambience, the complex is made up of two main sections, a Heritage Craft Gallery and Craft Village. Choose from the wide range of workshops or watch delightful musical performances and try out

authentic Johor cuisine.

chunk_text:
Muzium Tokoh gives an insight on the illustrious list of Johor's leaders and dignitaries, especially the Royal Family of Johor. Visitors can view a range of artefacts such as documents of the royal lineage. Housed in the Dato' Jaafar Building, the museum has a long history dating back to 1893. It was the official residence of the first Chief Minister of Johor, the late Dato' Jaafar bin Muhammad. The design concept of the building is similar to the Hardwick Hall in Derbyshire.

Learn Zapin, a Malay dance, or try out other great activities.

chunk_text: Johor Bahru Chinese Heritage Museum is housed in a restored four-storey shoplot, belonging to the prominent merchant Quok Keng Kang. The building was converted into the Chinese General Association during the Japanese Occupation in 1942, before it was renamed the Johor Bahru Tiong-Hua Association (JBTHA) in 1948. The building was renovated and officiated by the late Sultan Ismail in 1966. It was officially opened as a heritage museum in 2009.

chunk_text: Desaru Coast is a premium integrated destination resort comprising the Desaru Coast Adventure Waterpark, The Els Club Desaru Coast (a 45-hole golfing paradise), hotels and resorts. The waterpark offers rides and games for visitors of all ages. Be sure to try out the Tidal Wave Beach, one of the biggest wave pools in Southeast Asia. Don't miss Riptide, Kraken's Revenge, Wild Whirl, Surf Wall and many more rides for endless fun.

section: SULTAN ABU BAKAR MOSQUE Johor Bahru
chunk_text:
Built in 1892, this beautiful mosque is situated on a hill overlooking the Straits of Tebrau. Its design is influenced by Victorian and Mughal Indian architecture. Simple ornamentation on the arches resemble the Man Mandir Palace in Gwalior, India, while the twin columns at the façade depict Victorian architecture. The main prayer hall is rectangular in shape with a five-ridge roof known as 'Bumbung Perabung'. This mosque was commissioned by the late Sultan Abu Bakar, who was famed as the 'Father of Modern Johor'. Visitors are advised to dress modestly while visiting the mosque area.

chunk_text:
Situated in the heart of Southeast Asia, Malaysia is a vibrant destination with a diversity of cultures and traditions. This tropical paradise boasts pristine jungles and verdant national parks that are teeming with numerous species of birds and wildlife.

Malaysia's sun-drenched islands and beaches are home to a stunning range of marine life. Its natural wealth is complemented by magnificent modern landmarks and heritage buildings. There is something to charm every visitor, be it a history-lover, nature-enthusiast, sun-seeker or an avid shopper. Explore the length and breadth of the country to discover the many attractions of Malaysia!

chunk_text: Johor is Malaysia's southern gateway. Linked to Singapore via the Causeway (Tambak Johor) and the Second Link (LINKEDUA), its strategic location leads to its encouraging growth over the years, making it one of the country's most developed states. The state's wealth of natural attractions includes verdant rainforests, cascading waterfalls, thriving wetlands and mesmerising tropical islands. Comprising eight main districts, the state's vast landscape comprises sweeping plantations, well-manicured golf lawns, tranquil fishing villages, lush nature reserves and golden sandy beaches.

chunk_text: Johor Bahru is 330 km or a four-hour drive from Kuala Lumpur via the North-South Expressway. Both the JohorSingapore Causeway and the Second Link Expressway connect Singapore to Johor as well as the rest of the peninsula. Bus services to Johor from major cities and towns in the peninsula are available throughout the day. Tickets must be purchased early during peak seasons.

chunk_text:
Situated about two hours drive from Johor Bahru, Muar is a historical town and the capital city for the district of Muar. The town is also known as Bandar Maharani and has the distinction of being Johor's royal town. Muar's riverbank is the site of numerous interesting sights and scenes, from distinguished buildings to beautiful views of the sunset. One of the best ways to take in the views is by the Muar River Cruise. Enjoy unobstructed views of the Sultan Ibrahim Mosque, Sultan Ismail Bridge and Dataran Tanjung Emas which is famous for its seafood. The cruise departs from Jetty Tanjung Emas.

+6013-669 2263

chunk_text:
Kampung Sungai Melayu is a century-old Malay village that has been designated as an 'ecotourism village' by the state government. Surrounded by tropical vegetation, the village is an oasis of tranquility and greenery. Birdwatching enthusiasts will be happy to spot the variety of birdlife in the area. Take a short boat ride to the floating mussel farm or enjoy a mangrove tour for an interesting insight into the area's biodiversity. Overnight visitors can enjoy a more immersive experience through a homestay programme.
